item.title: Homogeneous Polynomial Carleson Operators Along the Paraboloid
item.description: arXiv:2611.05931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove boundedness on $L^p(\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$, $1<p<\infty$, of polynomial Carleson operators along the paraboloid with phase belonging to a class $Y$ of homogeneous polynomials. For $n,d\ge 2$, let $\mathcal{P}^{n,d}$ denote the class of all real-valued homogeneous polynomials in $n$ variables of degree $d$. We may take the class $Y$ to be an arbitrary linear subspace $Y \subseteq \mathcal{P}^{n,d}$ such that $\dim Y \le M_{n , d}$, where $M_{n , d}$ is a constant depending only on $n$ and $d$. The main novelty of our result is that we may allow a large collection of homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, in contrast to earlier results that relied on distinct degree assumptions. The heart of our proof is a $TT^*$ method, and the derivation of new estimates for oscillatory integral kernels involving interactions between homogeneous polynomial phases and the paraboloid.
item.dc:creator: Alina Zhu

item.title: Macroscopic return-time spectra and Hausdorff dimension transitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.06416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can the complete macroscopic spectrum of return times determine the Hausdorff dimension of the corresponding set of initial points? We classify all common lower and upper macroscopic intermediate-dimension spectra of zero-density integer sets and realize every admissible spectrum on a full-dimensional family of zero-frequency orbits under logarithmic-power bounds on inverse-branch contraction. For first-return branches with stretched-exponential contraction $e^{-n^\delta}$, $0<\delta<1$, complete spectrum levels exhibit a sharp zero/full dimension transition at the counting endpoint $\delta$. At the critical exponent, exact laws $N_y(t)\sim c_0t^\delta(\log t)^\beta$ yield zero dimension for $\beta\le0$ and full dimension for $\beta>0$, even with the complete spectrum fixed. An explicit two-branch intermittent interval map realizes this transition through genuine first returns. Above the critical exponent, imposing an exact counting law and a complete spectrum does not reduce the dimension of an intrinsic mean-energy level in an affine return tower. For nonlinear branches, we obtain quantitative bounds and an exact conditional-pressure formula under thermodynamic regularity assumptions, verified for an explicit non-affine family.
item.dc:creator: Jinjun Li

item.title: An equivalence principle for martingales
item.description: arXiv:2611.06426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that any discrete-time filtration can be embedded into a dyadic filtration, realized via a non-classical measure-preserving map. This embedding makes it possible to reduce certain problems involving vector-valued martingales to the case of Haar martingales. Some applications of this result will also be discussed.
item.dc:creator: Grigori A. Karagulyan, Linda A. Khachatryan, Khazhakanush V. Navoyan

item.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
item.description: arXiv:2611.05933v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that $b\in\mathrm{PCMO}$ (parabolic CMO space) if and only if $b\in L_\mathrm{loc}^1$ and the commutator $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$ is compact from $L^r(\omega^r)$ to $L^q(\omega^q)$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $1<r<q<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{q}=\alpha\in(0,1)$, and $\omega\in A_{r,q}^+(\gamma)$ (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where $I_\alpha^{\gamma+}$ is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space $\mathrm{PCMO}$ are also given. Our approach combines the unweighted compactness for mixed commutators, a local lower estimate for $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$, and both a quantitative Uchiyama-type description and the equivalence with $\inf_T\{\|[\cdot,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k-T\|_{L^r\to L^q}^\frac{1}{k}\}$ of $\mathrm{dist}_{\mathrm{PBMO}}(\cdot,\mathrm{PCMO})$, where the infimum is taken over all compact operators $T:L^r\to L^q$. Finally, we establish two parabolic weighted Fr\'echet--Kolmogorov compactness criteria, which further induce a parabolic interpolation theorem of compactness.
item.dc:creator: Mingming Cao, Weiyi Kong, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Chenfeng Zhu

item.title: Generalized principal eigenvalues for nonlocal operators with drift
item.description: arXiv:2611.06316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nonlocal diffusion operators with a drift term naturally arise in models such as moving coordinate systems induced by climate change. This paper systematically studies several concepts of generalized principal eigenvalues (GPEs) for such operators. We allow the dispersal kernel to be heterogeneous and non-symmetric, and remove the standard global upper bound on the kernel (thereby covering the case of heavy-tailed dispersal kernels). To overcome the analytical difficulties brought by this more general setting, we establish a new Harnack-type inequality for non-compactly supported kernels, and apply homogenization and cut-off approximation techniques to derive two-sided bounds for the domain approximation limit of GPEs. Furthermore, under the almost periodic setting, we prove that the GPEs defined through different admissible test function spaces (e.g., \(C^1\) spaces with bounded derivatives and uniformly continuous function spaces in the viscosity sense) are completely coincident. This characterization reveals a fundamental unification: the limit result of principal eigenvalues under domain approximation by Coville and Hamel coincides exactly with the explicit variational formula by Du, Fang, and Ni, thereby bridging two previously independent theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Hailin Tong, Tao Zhou

item.title: An Exact Poisson Mixture Representation of Siler Remaining Life Expectancy
item.description: arXiv:2611.06376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. No standard closed form is available for its remaining life expectancy, which must therefore be evaluated by numerical integration. We show that Siler remaining life expectancy at age $x$ is a Poisson mixture of Gompertz-Makeham remaining life expectancies, that is, a Poisson-weighted average of life expectancies in models with only a constant background hazard and an exponentially increasing senescence hazard. All components share the senescence hazard. Their background hazards increase from one component to the next by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines. The Poisson mean is the immaturity hazard that remains to be accumulated after age $x$. This representation yields an exact series of generalized exponential integrals with a closed-form bound on the truncation error. Replacing the background hazard by its discounted counterpart also gives the Laplace transform of the remaining lifetime. The mixture bounds the life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality: up to a term below the reciprocal of $a_2+b_1$, this loss equals the probability of an immaturity death times the life expectancy with the immaturity hazard removed. In annual Siler fits to Swedish female mortality, we estimate that the loss at birth fell from 4.3 years in 1900 to less than 0.01 years in 2020, which accounts for 15% of the gain in life expectancy at birth over the period.
item.dc:creator: Silvio C. Patricio

item.title: A property of boundary extensions of atomic singular inner functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.06877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using a property of the Hilbert transform, we prove a measure theoretic result concerning the extensions of atomic singular inner functions to the circle. Various alternative proofs are presented using the mean value theorem for harmonic functions and a well-known property of Blaschke products. Using the main result, we establish several facts concerning atomic singular inner functions and their logarithms.
item.dc:creator: Iason Efraimidis, Adrian Llinares, Sullivan MacDonald, Ignacio Uriarte-Tuero, Dragan Vukotic

item.title: Limit theorems for differential systems with multipoint boundary conditions in Sobolev spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.28267v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The most general class of multipoint inhomogeneous boundary-value problems for systems of linear ordinary differential equations of arbitrary order $r\geq 1$ is investigated, whose solutions belong to a given Sobolev space $W_p^{n+r}$, where $n\geq 0$ and $1\leq p\leq \infty$. The boundary conditions in these problems contain Caputo derivatives of fractional or integer orders, which may exceed the order of the differential system equations. Constructive sufficient conditions are established under which the solutions of these problems are continuous with respect to a parameter from an abstract metric space in the Sobolev space $W_p^{n+r}$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Complex Anal. Oper. Theory 20 (2026), Paper No. 173, 14 pp
item.dc:creator: Olena Atlasiuk, Vladimir Mikhailets

item.title: Pointwise Riesz potential bounds for rough singular integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.31888v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a complete characterization of the kernels $\Omega\in \Lup^1(\mathbb S^{d-1})$ for which the rough singular integral $\T_\Omega$ and its associated maximal operator $\M_\Omega$ satisfy pointwise bounds in terms of $\Int_1(|\nabla \cdot|)$ and $\M_1(|\nabla \cdot|)$, respectively, where $\Int_1$ is the Riesz potential and $\M_1$ is the fractional maximal operator. We show that these bounds hold if and only if $\Omega$ belongs to the homogeneous dual Sobolev space $\dot \W^{-1,\infty}(\mathbb S^{d-1})$. This characterization yields both a PDE characterization and a geometric characterization of the pointwise bounds. In the Lebesgue scale, we show that, for $d\geq 3$, every rough operator associated to a mean-zero kernel $\Omega\in\Lup^{d-1,\infty}(\mathbb S^{d-1})$ satisfies these pointwise bounds, and that the exponent $d-1$ is sharp. In dimension $d=2$, we use complex-analytic methods to establish a new pointwise bound in terms of the complex derivatives $\bar\partial f$ and $\partial f$, which are valid for every mean-zero $\Omega\in\Lup^1(\mathbb S^1)$. As a consequence, we obtain new Sobolev bounds for rough singular integrals in the plane.
item.dc:creator: Kabe Moen, Carlos P\'erez

item.title: Differentiation and Shift Property Characterisations of the Group Fourier Transform on the Heisenberg Group
item.description: arXiv:2610.40508v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, Krukowski characterised the Euclidean Fourier transform in terms of its behaviour with respect to differentiation. For locally compact abelian groups, he obtained a characterisation based on the behaviour of the Fourier transform under translation. Each of these results assumed that the operator (to be characterised) is an integral transform (with a kernel satisfying suitable regularity conditions), paired with a normalisation. In this paper, we obtain analogous results for the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group. Here, the differentiation property is formulated in terms of the behaviour of the group Fourier transform with respect to the left-invariant vector fields, and the shift property is on its behaviour under right translation. Both of these characterise the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group, once paired with a normalisation. Our results assume that the transform is continuous linear, and do not require it to be an integral transform a priori.
item.dc:creator: R. Lakshmi Lavanya

item.title: Parabolic Reifenberg Parametrizations and Corona Decompositions, with Applications to Singular Integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.42142v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For parabolic Ahlfors regular sets, we show that the bilateral weak geometric lemma (BWGL), bilateral approximation by unions of planes (BAUP), and corona decompositions by $Lip$(1,1/2) graphs (whose defining functions need not have half-order time derivatives in BMO) are equivalent. These geometric conditions do not imply the strong geometric lemma. A key tool is a parabolic version of Reifenberg's theorem for sets with holes, which we prove here. As an application of these geometric results, we prove that a parabolic Ahlfors $(n+2)$-regular measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, $1\leq n\leq d-1$, is parabolic uniformly rectifiable if its support satisfies any of these equivalent conditions and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(\mu)$.
item.dc:creator: John Hoffman, Matthew Hyde, Mihalis Mourgoglou

item.title: Some Characterisations of the Strichartz Fourier Transform on the Heisenberg Group
item.description: arXiv:2611.01128v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, Thangavelu introduced the Strichartz Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group. Around the same time, Krukowski characterised the classical Fourier transform on various settings, assuming a priori that the map is an integral transform, based on structural properties and a normalisation. In this paper, we obtain analogous results for the Strichartz Fourier transform, without assuming the characterised map is an integral transform. The spectral property is formulated jointly for the sublaplacian and central vector field, and the translation property uses a twisted form of left translation. The joint spectral property, the twisted translation property and a normalisation at one explicit test function, together characterise the transform on each ray of the Heisenberg fan. The twisted translation property, paired with a Dirac delta property, gives another characterisation. We characterise the radial kernel on each ray by a Laguerre-type differential equation. This gives a characterisation of the Hankel transform.
item.dc:creator: R. Lakshmi Lavanya

item.title: Distribution of mixed character sums and extremal problems for Littlewood polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2510.06161v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove distributional results for mixed character sums \begin{equation*}\sum_{n\le x }\chi(n)e(n\theta),\end{equation*} for fixed $\theta\in [0,1]$ and random character $\chi \pmod q$, as well as for a fixed character $\chi$ and randomly sampled $\theta\in [0,1].$ We present various applications of our results. For example, we construct Littlewood polynomials with large Mahler measure and $L_1$ norm, thus establishing new records in the Mahler and Newman problems. We also prove asymptotics for the $L_{2k}$ norms of well-known Turyn polynomials as $k\to\infty$, refuting a conjecture of G\"unther and Schmidt. An important ingredient in our work is a general way of dealing with "log-integrability" problems.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan W. Bober, Oleksiy Klurman, Besfort Shala

item.title: Schwarz $\mathrm{P}$ and Schwarz $\mathrm{D}$ as free-boundary minimal disks in a tetragonal disphenoid: exact areas
item.description: arXiv:2610.22013v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $T$ be the tetragonal disphenoid whose four congruent faces are isosceles triangles with sides $2,\sqrt3,\sqrt3$, so that the dihedral angles are $\pi/2$ along one opposite pair of edges and $\pi/3$ along the remaining four. By Smyth's theorem $T$ contains three embedded minimal disks meeting $\partial T$ orthogonally; the symmetry group $D_{2d}$ of $T$ fixes one and interchanges the other two. We identify all three completely. The distinguished disk is a patch of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{P}$ surface}$ and the congruent pair are patches of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{D}$ surface}$, with exact areas \[ \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{A}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} {K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} = 0.781700961348056\ldots, \] \[ \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{B}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} {2\,K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} = 0.639630785585503\ldots \] in the normalization $\operatorname{Vol}(T)=2/3$, inradius $r_T=\sqrt2/4$. In particular $2\,\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{A})\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{B})=1$, which we show is the Bonnet relation for the adjoint pair $(\mathrm{D},\mathrm{P})$. The proof is a reversal of the usual strategy: rather than uniformizing the Gauss map, we identify Smyth's three Plateau contours as the $\textit{tetrahedral four edges}$ and the $\textit{octahedral four edges}$ --- classically solved by $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ respectively --- and then conjugate. Both areas agree with Surface Evolver computations of Ken Brakke to all $15$ reported digits. We also show that all twelve corners of the three disks are midpoints of edges of $T$, each of the six midpoints being used twice, and that $T$ is precisely the alcove of the affine Weyl group $\widetilde{A}_{3}$, confirming a remark of Gandy, Cvijovi\'c, et al. (1999).
item.dc:creator: Steven Finch
